tagline: Around the Olympic Peninsula, from the Columbia's mouth to Olympia.
intro: US 101 comes into Washington on the Astoria-Megler Bridge, 4.1 miles over the Columbia near its mouth, and works north along Willapa Bay to Raymond and over the Willapa Hills to Aberdeen. Past Lake Quinault it runs 15 miles beside the Pacific by the beaches of Kalaloch, turns inland at Ruby Beach to follow the Hoh, and goes on through Forks and along Lake Crescent to Port Angeles, the northernmost point of its whole run.

From there it heads east past Sequim and its lavender fields and down Hood Canal, known for its oysters, through Brinnon and Hoodsport to Shelton and Olympia. Scenic Washington calls it way too long to do in one day.

moments.title: Ruby Beach
moments.text: Named for the ruby-like crystals in its sand, the beach is heaped with driftwood and set with sea stacks, and Destruction Island's lighthouse can be seen about four miles out.

moments.title: Forks
moments.text: Stephenie Meyer set Twilight here after searching Google for rainy settings, and the town's yearly visitors went from about 6,000 to nearly 73,000 by 2010.

moments.title: Lake Crescent
moments.text: A Klallam story has Mount Storm King throwing a boulder that cut Lake Sutherland in two, and many geologists think a great landslide about 8,000 years ago did much the same.
